links.note: Two failed monsoons changing what can be eaten turns on 30855 - climate determining what is grown. 30856 is the timing of the cropping calendar rather than the dependence on rainfall volume.
Classifying the state's crops into kharif, rabi and zaid is the seasonal cycle of 30856. (No model answer is stored.)
Dating rice cultivation in the Ganga plain to the 7th-8th millennium BCE is 30850's point that farming is among the oldest occupations.

Statement item on Harappan cultivation (the visible statement, that they knew no vegetables, is false) - the antiquity of Indian farming, 30850. DEFECT: statements 1-2 are missing from the stored stem.
Intercropping is one of the documented traditional practices of 30864; 30863 is the other named technique (terracing), and the set has no intercropping concept.
Surapala's Vrikshayurveda seed treatment is traditional practice recorded in an ancient text - 30864. 30849 mentions care with seed but as a quality of the farmer.
Why crops suit particular regions - 30855, where geography and climate determine the crop.
The count of agroclimatic zones follows from 30855's claim that varied geography and climate produce varied crops.
Zaid as the short summer season between the main crops - the seasonal cycle, 30856.
Kharif's dependence on the monsoon is 30856's point that the calendar is set by climate, not by the farmer.
'Haimana' as the older term for the winter crop - the cropping-season concept, 30856.
Matching kharif, rabi and zaid to monsoon, winter and summer - 30856.
Terracing against contour ploughing: 30863 is the terrace-farming concept (steps cut into the hillside, checking erosion and holding water).
Advantages of multiple cropping - traditional practice assessed on evidence, 30864, with the intercropping items.
The Kallanai as an ancient water-diverting work belongs to the traditional-practice material of 30864; this chapter's set has no irrigation concept.
Kalibangan as the site of early intercropping evidence - the antiquity of Indian farming, 30850.
Fifteen agroclimatic zones - 30855.
The southwest monsoon's June-September window is what sets the kharif season - 30856.
The three cropping seasons named - 30856.
Intercropping named as the ancient practice - 30864.
Barley and millet at Mehrgarh in the 7th millennium BCE - 30850's antiquity claim.
Thar arid against Himalayan alpine - the climatic variety of 30855 that decides what can be farmed.
The Arabic origin of kharif, rabi and zaid - the cropping-season vocabulary of 30856.
